content.comment_body: I understand that SVV-cable (0.8mm²) is typically recommended for connections between modules and switches. I have installed CAT5 cables for all my switches—can I still use the [product_name] system for home automation?

I don't see any issue with using a CAT5 cable. According to the manual (page 276), each input uses a current greater than 2mA, and I assume your voltage is 24V. If your CAT5 cables support these specifications, then it should work fine. You can find the manual at [url].

analysis.insight_summary: Users are asking whether CAT5 cables can be used to connect switches with the [product_name] system instead of the standard SVV-cable. The reply provides technical confirmation that CAT5 cables are suitable if they meet the required voltage and current ratings, referencing the product manual. Users want assurance and clear guidance when choosing alternative installation materials and value official documentation for validation.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] system to operate properly with widely-available cables like CAT5, even if those differ from standard recommendations, and look for confirmation of compatibility.
